body.statement: Theorem 1 (Law-invariant RankPeel reconstruction on complete runs). For every \((G,P)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{PNHZ}}\), if every measured endpoint pair adaptively requested by \(\operatorname{RankPeel}(P_X,R^{\mathrm{law}}_{P_X})\) belongs to \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{stab}}(P_X)\), then RankPeel terminates with \(\widehat G\) satisfying \([\widehat G]=\theta_G\). It recovers the same full binary adjacency matrix identified by Theorem 3 of Prashant et al., with only within-layer latent-label permutations, but replaces their exhaustive subset construction by deterministic pairwise pure-block tests and representative-neutrality deletion over measured pure-descendant surrogates.
body.justification: The theorem converts same-class identification into a deterministic pairwise and deletion protocol whenever the observed law fixes every requested derivative rank.
body.gap: Prashant et al. already identify the full binary adjacency matrix and already use measured pure descendants as higher-layer surrogates, but their exhaustive subset construction has no deterministic quadratic observed-query guarantee.
body.consumer: The theorem gives latent-hierarchy researchers a canonical complete-run population benchmark with an explicit list of observed-law queries.
